Dashboard preview draws the current reality tree flat, ignoring its cause links
description:
Symptom (Rufus, 2026-09-26): the dashboard preview of ltp/rufus-david-collab/rufus-david-collab.ltp.yaml shows the current reality view as one flat row of cards, with no structure or edges, although the YAML has a real tree.

Data is fine (verified): the current_reality view has 38 entities and 25 relationships, all same-view with valid kinds: 18 contributes_to (a chain down to r-e-not-adopted, with loops through r-e-only-own-time), 4 challenges, 2 supersedes, 1 supports. No 'causes' links. 13 entities are unlinked (situation observations), which is expected.

Pipeline: skills/ltp-project/scripts/preview_dashboard.py (added by David in 'clean up skills', docs in skills/ltp-project/references/preview.md; see also skills/ltp-visualize/SKILL.md) converts the interchange YAML into the older dashboard model and serves or exports dashboard/index.html. Run: python3 skills/ltp-project/scripts/preview_dashboard.py ltp/rufus-david-collab/rufus-david-collab.ltp.yaml [--export-html]. convert() passes every relationship through as a link (RELATIONS maps contributes_to -> contributes_to, challenges, supersedes, supports) and lists them in views['current-reality'].links, so the links reach the model. The flattening is therefore most likely in dashboard/index.html's layout for the current-reality view.

Hypotheses to check, in order: (1) the layout only ranks nodes by certain relations (e.g. 'causes', or relations it knows from the old model) and ignores contributes_to; (2) it lays out by parent/child rather than by links; (3) it expects old-model entity types (ROLE_TYPES maps intermediate_cause -> root_cause; undesirable_effect, root_cause, evidence, observation pass through) and something about the types breaks ranking; (4) the cycles (only-own-time -> product-unclear -> ... -> only-own-time, and only-own-time <-> no-funding-applied) break a layered layout, so it falls back to a flat row. Quick test for (4): export with the two loop-closing links removed (r-rel-own-time-drives-product-unclear, r-rel-own-time-drives-no-funding) and see whether structure appears. Compare with the other views (goal tree uses parent_designation_id and necessary_for; does it render as a tree?).

Also noted: rufus-david-collab.dashboard-preview.html is committed and was regenerated locally (uncommitted) — decide whether generated previews belong in the repo.

Done when: the current reality view shows the causal structure (undesirable effects foregrounded, causes below, loops visible), and a note in preview.md says how cycles and non-'causes' kinds are drawn. Related friction: ltp/rufus-david-collab/friction-log.md (salient node types not foregrounded).

title: Research: YAML-driven static dashboard (JS loads .ltp.yaml at runtime) to replace ltp-visualize export
description: Today skills/ltp-visualize runs skills/ltp-project/scripts/preview_dashboard.py --export-html, which bakes the YAML into a standalone HTML at export time. Every YAML edit means re-exporting, and it needs PyYAML (system Python blocked by PEP 668 — had to use a venv). Research converting this to a fixed, versioned JS dashboard that fetches/parses the .ltp.yaml in the browser, so editing the YAML and refreshing is enough.
design: Questions to answer: (1) How much of preview_dashboard.py's transform (YAML -> dashboard data shape, display defaults, omissions per skills/ltp-project/references/preview.md) can be ported to JS? (2) YAML parsing in-browser (js-yaml, vendored vs CDN). (3) Loading the file: fetch() fails on file:// so need a tiny local server, file picker/drag-drop, or a hybrid (embed default + reload from picker). (4) Reuse of the existing Reason Commons dashboard UI code vs a new standalone viewer. (5) Where the JS lives (versioned in repo, e.g. skills/ltp-visualize/ or a top-level viewer/), and how the skill just opens it with a YAML path. (6) Live reload on YAML change. Output: short findings note with recommended approach and effort estimate (S/M/L), then follow-up implementation bead if worthwhile.
acceptance_criteria: Findings note in repo (or bead notes) with recommended approach, file:// loading solution, effort estimate, and go/no-go for implementation.
notes: Leaning approach (2026-09-26): local server. Skill runs 'python3 -m http.server' at repo root and opens viewer.html?src=<path-to-.ltp.yaml>; fetch() works (file:// blocks fetch even for same-dir siblings), refresh/poll gives live reload, no PyYAML needed. Fallback: file picker / File System Access API handle with a reload button. Still to check: how much display logic in preview_dashboard.py must be ported to JS.
